product_one_liner.value: Owl provides insurance-native AI that reads and structures entire claim files, surfaces cited evidence and signals, and answers questions for insurers’ claims teams, adjusters, investigators, legal teams and underwriters.

pricing_page.notes: The public site presents product and contact/briefing routes but no public pricing page or priced plans.

named_customers.notes: The public success-story page and case study describe customers only generically (for example, a leading insurer), without naming at least two customers; partners do not count.

employee_band.notes: The cited company profile reports 92 employees.

eng_blog.notes: The readable resource index is a marketing and industry-content library; it does not show an engineering/technical blog with at least two build-focused posts by engineers.

public_docs.notes: The documentation site lists getting-started, core-concepts, API-reference, integrations, security/compliance, data-taxonomy, model-card and changelog sections.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The careers page lists open roles, but none of the titles is AI, ML, machine learning, data science, applied scientist, research scientist, NLP, LLM or computer vision.

model_provider.notes: Public materials describe Owl’s own insurance/domain models and benchmark comparisons, but do not clearly state a production third-party model provider.

raised_18mo.notes: The latest identified round was the $30M Series B announced in November 2021, before the 18-month window beginning 2025-05-09.

launched_6mo.notes: Owl’s page dated 2026-05-09 introduces Template Assistant as a new feature, within the six months before 2026-11-09.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: The public team/about page identifies leadership and roles but does not provide sufficiently dated join/leave information to establish a C-level or VP-level change in the window.
